probes.timeoutJustification: L5 is the UI canary and it runs first. The questions are all post-boot: the csregister epoch counters only move once the component system has registered and a space change has happened, the browser panel only exists after the UI module's band-3 registration, and DL-03's cursor and click question needs a drawn window. None of that is inside the attach window. The number is the observer's own budget: bootstrap and boot, then the level the profile loads, over which the arm opens the replay browser through ui::OpenBrowser, then a 180 s observation during which the SURVIVE arm files a heartbeat and a provisional record every second, so a process that dies at 40 s leaves 40 s on disk instead of a silence. replay-local-bare carries an OfflineMechanism and all four loopback pins, which is what allows a window past the attach one at all.
probes.scope: EVERY CLAIM FROM THIS LAUNCH IS A CLAIM ABOUT probe_replay.dll, NOT ABOUT echoreplay.dll. The two binaries are compiled from the same sources - tests/replay/check.ps1 asserts that against CMake's own manifest, both directions - and they differ by one translation unit, an output name and nothing else that has ever been measured. That is strictly stronger than wave 1's per-subsystem probes and strictly weaker than launching the shipped DLL, and the launch that runs echoreplay.dll itself remains owed. The observer WATCHES: it re-implements no product path, so a green here is a statement about the shipped code, and a red here is a defect in it.
probes.why: The cheapest launch that executes src/ui/csregister.cpp in the shipped path, on the least-proven precondition in the wave. The BROWSER arm is selected by ECHOREPLAY_OPEN naming a DIRECTORY, which replay-local-bare's Env block supplies; an empty value is refused by the module rather than being read as a third meaning. exclusive is true and it is not a formality: probe_replay carries src/bootstrap/bootstrap.cpp and src/engine/tick.cpp, so a second bootstrap-carrying plugin in the same install loses the instance claim, installs nothing and files nothing - the observer reports what it found beside it in the record's coexist field so that outcome is on disk rather than inferred from a silence.

probes.timeoutJustification: The capture half is a match-time measurement by definition: the fifteen live-session reads of the plan's group A need a loaded level and a live session, and the file this launch exists to produce is a recording of one. The number is the capture window plus the boot ahead of it: ECHOREPLAY_CAPTURE_SECS in capture-local's Env block closes the file from inside the process, and the harness waits for the module's own closed: line before taskkill, so the window has to hold boot, the level load, the capture seconds and the close.
probes.scope: As above: a claim about probe_replay.dll. Additionally, this launch produces F-REAL, and the capture is the product's own writer running in the product's own code path - the observer does not write a capture and does not touch the transport.
probes.why: The first launch in this project's history to run the shipped module set, and the only wave-2 launch that writes a capture. It answers whether the product survives a real session and it produces the file L4 and LF are about.

probes.timeoutJustification: The playback battery cannot start before DurationUs() is non-zero, which needs a loaded level and a loaded file, and every read in it - the seek battery, the pause question, the audio reconcile, the netvar and roster lines - is measured against a running transport. The window is boot, load, the battery, and the observation the plan sizes at 285 s for this profile.
probes.scope: A claim about probe_replay.dll, on F-SYNTH. F-SYNTH is a constructed file: a read that answers here answers about the product's handling of a file built to the format's rules, not about a capture of a real match. That is what the L4 differential is for, and a read that answers differently on the two is a capture-fidelity finding.
probes.why: The playback battery on the synthetic fixture, independent of whether L2 succeeded, because F-SYNTH is on disk before the launch. ECHOREPLAY_OPEN names a FILE, which selects the PLAYBACK arm.

probes.scope: A claim about probe_replay.dll, on F-REAL. It is the milestone launch, and it is only interpretable beside L3: the same battery, the same binary, a different file.
probes.why: The real capture L2 produced, played in a real game, read differentially against L3.

probes.timeoutJustification: LF's arm. Same profile and same file as W2-R-playback-real, and the same completion point -- the file playing out. The window is the file's length plus boot, and it is attended, so it must not be shortened: a human is watching it and the launch is the one the fidelity question is asked on.
probes.scope: A claim about probe_replay.dll, on F-REAL. It is the milestone launch, and it is only interpretable beside L3: the same battery, the same binary, a different file. PLAYBACK-IDLE additionally samples nothing a human's seeking would perturb and never drives the transport itself, so its rows are the subset of the playback battery that needs no command: the 4b pause proof and the 0.5x audio slope are NOT in its list, because asking them would mean driving the transport out from under the person watching.
probes.why: The fidelity arm (15.5). The arm is selected by the DESCRIPTOR's probe id ending in -idle, not by a machine-wide variable and not by the file: nothing carries `attended` to the module, and keying on the id the harness already hands us in REPLAY_PROBE_IDS keeps the arm a property of this launch's row (RK-11).
